plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 1.1.4
plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating the limiting definition of a tangent line. Panel (a): a smooth curve in the xy-plane with a fixed point P and a moveable point Q marked on the curve; multiple pink secant lines through P fan outward, converging toward a limiting position labeled Tangent line, with arrows indicating the rotational approach to the limit. Panel (b): the same construction applied to a circle, showing P and Q on the circle with multiple secant lines rotating toward the tangent line at P. The figure establishes the general definition of a tangent line as the limiting position of secant lines as Q approaches P along the curve, and confirms that this definition agrees with the classical tangent to a circle.

interactionPlan.concept: The tangent line to a curve at point P is the limiting position of the secant line through P and Q as point Q approaches P along the curve.
elements: x and y axes with labels 'x' and 'y' (for general curve)
Blue path representing the curve or circle
Pink tangent line at point P, labeled 'Tangent line'
Pink moving secant line through points P and Q, labeled 'Secant line'
Light gray curved arrow indicating the rotational approach of the secant line to the tangent line
Faded pink secant lines and blue dots showing previous positions of Q (static background context)
Text annotation showing the current slope of the secant/tangent line

interactions.label: Curve shape
interactions.teaches: The limit definition of a tangent line applies universally to smooth curves, naturally extending the classical definition for a circle.

interactions.label: Distance of Q from P
interactions.teaches: As the distance between Q and P shrinks to zero, the secant line rotates and converges to a single limiting position: the tangent line.

interactions.label: Position of P
interactions.teaches: The tangent line represents the instantaneous direction of the curve, which changes smoothly as P moves along the curve.

demo_steps.title: The secant line
demo_steps.narration: A secant line passes through a fixed point P and another point Q on the curve. Its slope represents the average rate of change between these two points.

demo_steps.title: Taking the limit
demo_steps.narration: Slide Q closer to P. As Q approaches P, the secant line rotates. The limiting position it reaches when Q meets P is the tangent line.

demo_steps.title: Moving point P
demo_steps.narration: Change the position of P. The tangent line's slope updates, showing how the instantaneous direction varies along the curve.

demo_steps.title: Consistency with circles
demo_steps.narration: Switching to a circle shows that this limit definition perfectly matches the classical idea of a tangent line touching the circle at a single point.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A tangent line is not just a line that 'touches at one point', but the ultimate limit of a secant line as the two points of intersection merge into one.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Render the generic curve as a smooth polynomial (e.g., cubic) in the first quadrant with visible x/y axes. The circle should be centered in the view without axes. Use blue for the curve/circle and points, and pink/magenta for lines. Keep the faded traces of intermediate Q points and their secant lines to mimic the static figure's sense of motion. The curved arrow should be a thick, semi-transparent gray gradient pointing from the furthest secant to the tangent line. Display the active slope as a small numeric readout.

authoredContext: To obtain a definition of a tangent line that applies to curves other than circles, we must view tangent lines another way. For this purpose, suppose that we are interested in the tangent line at a point P on a curve in the xy-plane and that Q is any point that lies on the curve and is different from P. The line through P and Q is called a secant line for the curve at P. Intuition suggests that if we move the point Q along the curve toward P, then the secant line will rotate toward a limiting position. The line in this limiting position is what we will consider to be the tangent line at P (Figure 1.1.4a). As suggested by Figure 1.1.4b, this new concept of a tangent line coincides with the traditional concept when applied to circles.

discrepancies: The labels 'Tangent line' and 'Secant line' are colored pink and purple in the generated figure, whereas they are black in the source image.
The 'Tangent line' and 'Secant line' labels in the generated figure overlap with the y-axis, curve, and secant lines, whereas the source places them cleanly in empty space.
The rotational sweep arrow in the generated figure uses a thin line with a standard triangle head, whereas the source uses a thick, stylized, outlined white block-arrow.
The shaded wedge area between the lines in the generated figure uses a solid flat color with opacity, whereas the source uses a smooth gradient fading out from the intersection point P.
